# Assets

## The short version

**The game needs none.** Every surface is generated by `TextureFactory`, every sound by
`ProceduralAudio`, every mesh by `MeshBuilder`. A fresh clone is playable and coherent
with nothing downloaded.

Downloaded packs *replace* the generated versions by name, with no code change. That is
the whole design of the pipeline: the project is complete without them and materially
better with them.

---

## How the override works

### Textures

`MaterialLibrary` resolves each surface in three steps:

1. `Resources/Art/<Name>_Albedo` (+ optional `_Normal`, `_MaskMap`) — a downloaded set
2. failing that, a generated albedo from `TextureFactory`
3. failing even a shader, an unlit fallback so nothing renders magenta

So to use a downloaded texture set, put it here:

```
Assets/Game/Resources/Art/
    CaveRock_Albedo.png
    CaveRock_Normal.png
    CaveRock_MaskMap.png
    Shotcrete_Albedo.png
    ...
```

The names come from the `SurfaceKind` enum: `CaveRock`, `CaveRockDamp`, `Shotcrete`,
`SteelPainted`, `SteelRusted`, `ArcadeCarpet`, `Decking`.

Set the normal map's import type to **Normal map** and the mask map's to **Default**
with sRGB **off**. Once `_Albedo` exists the library switches that surface over on the
next play, and *Asset Fetcher → Check what is wired up* will confirm it.

> **Why no generated normal maps?** A runtime-created `Texture2D` cannot be marked as a
> normal map, and the packing Unity's shaders expect differs by platform — so a
> generated "normal map" would be silently wrong somewhere. Surface relief in the
> generated path comes from geometry and vertex colour instead. Real tangent-space maps
> arrive with downloaded packs, which import through the normal pipeline and are
> correct.

### Audio

Drop a clip into `Assets/Game/Resources/Audio/` named after the key and
`AudioDirector` uses it instead of the synthesised version:

```
GeneratorHum   FanLoop      PumpLoop     Cavitation
Static         CaveAmbience Drip         MetalImpact
DoorCycle      BreakerClack Footstep     Jumpscare
DawnChime
```

Loops need to actually loop. The synthesised versions are made seamless with an
equal-power crossfade of the tail over the head; a downloaded clip has to be trimmed
properly or it will click once a second.

### Models

The cast is generated by `AnimatronicFactory` and needs no downloaded models.

To use sculpted characters instead, replace `AnimatronicModelSpawner` with a prefab
reference and keep an `AnimatronicRig` component with its bone fields wired.
`ServoAnimator` drives the rig by **reference**, not by name lookup, so any rig works
once the fields are assigned.

---

## The fetcher

*Tools → Grotto → Asset Fetcher* reads `Assets/Game/AssetManifest.json` and downloads
into `Assets/Game/Art/Downloaded/<id>/`, which is gitignored.

Two things it does that a naive downloader would not:

**It refuses to extract outside its target directory.** Zip entries can contain `../`
paths; extracting them blindly ("zip slip") lets a malicious archive write anywhere the
editor can. Every entry path is resolved and checked before a byte is written.

**It records attribution as it goes.** An `ATTRIBUTION.md` is written beside the
downloads with the source, licence and URL of everything pulled — because the moment to
record that is at download time, not the week before release.

### About the `UNVERIFIED` markers

Entries whose `verified` flag is `false` use the documented public URL pattern for that
source, but the URL could not be confirmed: the machine this project was authored on had
no network egress to any art host. If a download fails, click **Open source page** and
fetch the file by hand — the manifest carries a browse URL for every entry.

## Recommended sources

| Source | Licence | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| [ambientCG](https://ambientcg.com) | CC0 | PBR surfaces — rock, concrete, metal, carpet, wood |
| [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com) | CC0 | HDRIs, textures, models; has a clean public API |
| [Kenney](https://kenney.nl) | CC0 | Props, UI, audio |
| [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com) | CC0 | Stylised models |
| [Sonniss GDC Bundle](https://sonniss.com/gameaudiogdc) | Royalty-free | Enormous, excellent SFX library |
| [Freesound](https://freesound.org) | Varies — filter to CC0 | Cave tone, drips, machinery |

---

## Before you ship

1. Read `Assets/Game/Art/Downloaded/ATTRIBUTION.md`.
2. Confirm every licence permits your distribution. CC0 needs no attribution but giving
   it is polite; CC-BY **requires** it; Sonniss' bundle has its own terms.
3. Put the credits somewhere a player can reach them.
4. `MIT` in `LICENSE` covers the **code and design documents only**. It does not cover
   anything the fetcher downloaded.

## On Five Nights at Freddy's assets

Do not add them. FNAF characters, models, audio, likenesses and trademarks are Scott
Cawthon's intellectual property, and ripped assets are not licensed for redistribution
under any circumstances.

This project is an original game that borrows the genre's structural ideas — a
stationary night shift, resource attrition, surveillance, scheduled AI aggression — and
none of its content. Keeping it that way is what makes it yours to release.
